text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1: spike in 502/504 + elevated p99 latency for service `redwood-inference-api` in eu-west-1a; synthetic checks failing; NLB target flapping observed. PagerDuty PD-4821. Channel created #incidents. thread_ts=1768012345

alex (oncall): I\u2019m on it. Paging @kevin-runtime and @tanvi-netops. Setting myself as incident commander. :rotating_light:

kevin-runtime: Ack. Looking at runtime logs — seeing repeated TCP RSTs and ENI detach/attach chatter from a small set of hosts in eu-west-1a. KV cache pressure spikes correlate with the tail latencies.

tanvi-netops: Confirmed via cloud metrics: ENI events and host retransmits concentrated in a placement group. Opening AWS case 123456789. Also seeing brief control-plane heartbeat misses for a subset of hypervisors.

alex (oncall): Short-term plan: 1) shed traffic off eu-west-1a to other AZs/regions, 2) increase NLB deregistration grace/health-check thresholds to stop flapping, 3) throttle heavy generation routes on eu-west-1a to limit cache churn. @kevin-runtime can you run 1 & 3 now?

kevin-runtime: Starting traffic shift. Using router CLI to move 30% to eu-west-1b and 20% to eu-west-2:

```
# shift small portion off eu-west-1a
redwood-trafficctl split --service redwood-inference-api --from eu-west-1a --to eu-west-1b=30 --to eu-west-2=20
```

kevin-runtime: Also adding soft QoS on heavy model routes to cut sustained KV churn:

```
redwood-config set-rate --route /v1/generate?model=gpt-large-quant --region eu-west-1a --max-qps 10
```

maria-sales: FYI support is getting inbound from two enterprise tenants reporting 5xx errors for EU inference calls. They want ETA. I\u2019ll draft customer-facing note once we confirm mitigation. cc @dylan-support

dylan-support: Roger. Please include affected tenant IDs in the comms and we\u2019ll spin up a bridge if any are high-touch.

kevin-runtime: After initial shift: error rate for the service dropped from ~5% -> ~2% in 10 minutes. Rerouted traffic p95 latency down from ~820ms -> ~360ms. Still seeing RSTs on a small host subset.

tanvi-netops: Adjusting NLB target-group settings: deregistration delay -> 300s, health-check interval -> 20s, healthy threshold 3 -> this should reduce churn while AWS investigates.

alex (oncall): Good. I\u2019ll escalate the AWS case and add @eng-ops to the bridge.

eng-bot: aws-case-updated: 123456789 -> logs attached for hosts 10.0.1.12, 10.0.1.13 (eu-west-1a). AWS acknowledged elevated facility-level networking activity and is investigating host isolation.

kevin-runtime: Noticing cascade: KV cache invalidations are triggering cold-starts for model shards. Enabling local prefix cache to reduce cross-host fetches:

```
redwood-kvctl enable-prefix-cache --region eu-west-1a --routes '/v1/*' --ttl 60s
```

tanvi-netops: AWS: "we see sporadic control-plane heartbeat misses impacting a subset of hypervisors in eu-west-1a; mitigation in progress to isolate faulty hosts." No firm ETA yet.

alex (oncall): Incident state: partial impact limited to eu-west-1a. Global service remains up thanks to routing. Mitigation in progress. Handing ownership: @kevin-runtime takes owner for ongoing mitigation; I remain IC for comms.

kevin-runtime: Taking owner. Next step: drain and standby the problematic instances and continue shifting traffic off the AZ if necessary.

kevin-runtime: Draining hosts (in-flight connections will 502 if they hit drained ones):

```
redwood-nodectl drain --region eu-west-1a --filter 'host in (10.0.1.12,10.0.1.13,10.0.1.14)'
```

dylan-support: Sent initial customer update to affected enterprises explaining partial impact and that traffic is being routed to healthy AZs. Asked them to open tickets if they still see failures.

maria-sales: Also flagged one SAML-auth tenant where a scheduled job timed out. Suggested SDK-level idempotent retries to them as a workaround.

kevin-runtime: 35 minutes after alert: overall error rate ~0.7%, eu-west-1a p99 trending down. Residual 502s are from in-flight requests to drained hosts.

tanvi-netops: AWS updated: host isolation complete and data-plane migration from faulty hypervisors in progress. They recommend keeping NLB grace elevated for ~1 hour.

alex (oncall): Keep elevated NLB/health settings for 60 minutes. Kevin: if metrics stay steady for 30m, start reverting throttles and cache TTL to defaults.

eng-bot: monitoring-alert-created: alert_id=A-3302 (p99>1.5s or error_rate>1.5%).

kevin-runtime: 30m steady state reached. Reverting soft throttles and TTLs:

```
redwood-config set-rate --route /v1/generate?model=gpt-large-quant --region eu-west-1a --max-qps 200
redwood-kvctl set-ttl --region eu-west-1a --routes '/v1/*' --ttl 300s
```

kevin-runtime: Final verification: error rate stable at ~0.2%, p95 back to baseline. Drained hosts have been rehomed to healthy hypervisors.

alex (oncall): Closing timeline: incident will be closed in 10m barring regressions. Postmortem owners: @kevin-runtime (eng-runtime), @tanvi-netops (netops). Deliverables: timeline, root cause (AWS control-plane heartbeat misses -> host network degradation), impacted tenant list, and follow-ups (NLB config hardening, cross-AZ warm pool sizing, enhanced synthetics for early detection).

maria-sales: I\u2019ll prepare customer-facing summary and coordinate with support for affected accounts.

dylan-support: Handing back to oncall rotation. Reopen if anything pops. :white_check_mark:

alex (oncall): Incident resolved. last_message_ts=1768015945. Thanks everyone. :tada:
